Deploys changes from the selected cPanel-managed repository. Deployment requires a valid checked-in .cpanel.yml in the top-level directory, one or more local or remote branches, and a clean working tree. Pulling uses --ff-only: HEAD must already be up to date or capable of fast-forwarding. Failed prerequisites disable deployment functionality and hide deployment information.
The response fields are optional. Task IDs, log paths and SSE URLs are payload data; request success does not establish deployment completion and the client does not follow or poll them.

The reviewer observed integer deploy_id and a floating-point queued timestamp after a deployment was queued. Preserve the documented string alternatives unchanged and accept integer identifiers and finite numeric queued timestamps without coercion. A payload mismatch can occur after queuing; do not retry it as though nothing happened.

For a non-deployable repository the reviewer observed status 1 with explicit null data and no deployment queued. This result returns null. An absent data member remains a payload mismatch, and a non-null task result still does not establish deployment completion.

Deployment requires a checked-in top-level .cpanel.yml, branches and a clean working tree; otherwise the server hides deployment information and disables deployment functionality.

All row fields are optional. deploy_id and repository_state.date retain their pinned integer contracts, also reported as integers by the reviewer. A status timestamp is returned only when that state occurred according to the pinned source. Preserve omission and do not infer nullable fields.

Task IDs, log paths and SSE URLs remain payload data. Request success means the status request succeeded, not that deployment succeeded; inspect task state separately. The client performs no polling, log reads or SSE connections.

The reviewer observed floating-point active, queued and succeeded timestamps. Those three fields preserve documented strings unchanged and additionally accept finite JSON numbers without coercion. Unobserved canceled and failed timestamps retain their string contracts; their numeric variants need separate evidence.
